Look up the original names of loci and chromosomes stored as integers

Source: R/loci_sidecar.R
gt_lookup_loci.Rd

With names_as_int = TRUE and chromosomes_as_int = TRUE, gen_tibble() stores the names of the loci, and their chromosomes, as integers, to save memory and time with large datasets (e.g. RAD loci assembled de novo, with millions of loci, each its own "chromosome"). The original names are written to sidecar files next to the backing file (see Details), from which these functions get them back:

  • gt_lookup_loci() gives back the original names and chromosomes of some loci (e.g. the hits of a selection scan), without changing the gen_tibble;

  • gt_lookup_chromosomes() gives back the names of chromosome codes (e.g. the chromosome column of the results of window statistics or runs of homozygosity);

  • gt_restore_loci() puts the original names back into the loci table of a gen_tibble (e.g. once it has been filtered down to fewer loci).

Usage

gt_lookup_loci(.x, loci, check_positions = TRUE)

gt_lookup_chromosomes(.x, chromosomes)

gt_restore_loci(.x, names = TRUE, chromosomes = TRUE, check_positions = TRUE)

Arguments

.x

a gen_tibble (or, except for gt_restore_loci(), its genotypes column)

loci

a subset of the loci table of .x: rows of show_loci(), in any order, possibly with extra columns (e.g. the statistics of a scan); or row numbers of show_loci(.x), as given by which().

check_positions

boolean: whether to check that the positions of the loci in the locus sidecar are the same as in loci (or in the loci table of .x, for gt_restore_loci()). For gt_lookup_loci(), they are only checked if loci has a position column. Default is TRUE.

chromosomes

for gt_lookup_chromosomes(), a vector of chromosome codes (e.g. the chromosome column of the results of windows_pairwise_pop_fst() or gt_roh_window()); for gt_restore_loci(), boolean: whether to restore the names of the chromosomes (if they are integer codes), default TRUE.

names

boolean: whether to restore the names of the loci (if they are integers). Default is TRUE.

Value

gt_lookup_loci() returns loci (as a table), with integer names in its name column, and integer codes in its chromosome column, replaced by their original names (as character vectors); the other columns, and the rows and their order, are unchanged. Columns that already hold names are left as they are, so the same code works on data read with or without the integer options.

gt_lookup_chromosomes() returns the names of the chromosomes (a character vector, with NA for NA). Chromosomes that are already names (a factor or a character vector) are returned as a character vector.

gt_restore_loci() returns .x, with the original names in its loci table (as if it had been read without the integer options: names as a character vector, and chromosomes as a factor). It does not save it: use gt_save().

Details

The sidecars of the backing file foo.bk are:

  • foo.loci.tsv (written with names_as_int = TRUE), with the columns int_name, name, chromosome and position, and one line per locus, in increasing order of integer name. The names are those that names_as_int = FALSE would give (with a missing ID replaced by the chromosome and position), and the chromosomes are their names (not their codes);

  • foo.chromosomes.tsv (written with chromosomes_as_int = TRUE), with the columns int_chromosome and chromosome, and one line per chromosome, in increasing order of code.

Both are tab separated text files with a header, with no quotes, and "." for missing values, so they can be read with any tool (e.g. data.table::fread(path, quote = "") or readr::read_tsv(path, quote = "")), and joined to show_loci() by name = int_name or chromosome = int_chromosome.

The sidecars are written by gen_tibble() when it reads a VCF file with parser = "cpp", and by gt_merge_vcfs() and gt_concat_vcfs(). Functions that write a new backing file (gt_update_backingfile(), gt_order_loci(), rbind()) write new sidecars for it, with the loci and chromosomes that they keep (integer names and codes keep their values, so they still find their line). Keep the sidecars with the other files of the gen_tibble (see gt_save()): without them, the original names are lost.

Only the file name ties a sidecar to its data, so the position of each locus in the locus sidecar is compared with its position in the loci table: a different position means that the sidecar belongs to other data (e.g. files copied by hand from different runs), and is an error. If you changed the positions of the loci yourself (e.g. after a liftover to a new assembly), the names in the sidecar are still right: use check_positions = FALSE. The chromosome sidecar has no positions to check.

Lookups are fast: the first lookup in a session reads through a sidecar once to index it (about a second per GB), and later lookups of a few loci only read the parts of the file that hold them.

Examples

vcf_path <- system.file(
  "extdata/anolis/punctatus_t70_s10_n46_filtered.recode.vcf.gz",
  package = "tidypopgen"
)
anole_gt <- gen_tibble(vcf_path,
  backingfile = tempfile("anolis_"),
  names_as_int = TRUE, chromosomes_as_int = TRUE, quiet = TRUE
)
head(show_loci(anole_gt))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   big_index  name chromosome position genetic_dist allele_ref allele_alt
#>       <int> <int>      <int>    <int>        <dbl> <chr>      <chr>     
#> 1         1     1          1        2            0 G          A         
#> 2         2     2          1       13            0 A          G         
#> 3         3     3          1       16            0 T          C         
#> 4         4     4          2       57            0 G          A         
#> 5         5     5          3       34            0 T          C         
#> 6         6     6          3       37            0 A          C         

# the original names of the loci with the most missing genotypes
missing <- loci_missingness(anole_gt)
gt_lookup_loci(anole_gt, which(missing > 0.6))
#> # A tibble: 81 × 7
#>    big_index name         chromosome position genetic_dist allele_ref allele_alt
#>        <int> <chr>        <chr>         <int>        <dbl> <chr>      <chr>     
#>  1        25 locus_2327_… locus_2327       59            0 A          C         
#>  2        71 locus_6428_… locus_6428       40            0 C          T         
#>  3        73 locus_6428_… locus_6428       42            0 T          G         
#>  4       236 locus_19280… locus_192…        4            0 G          T         
#>  5       254 locus_19654… locus_196…       88            0 C          A         
#>  6       255 locus_19654… locus_196…       89            0 C          A         
#>  7       256 locus_19654… locus_196…       90            0 A          T         
#>  8       349 locus_21964… locus_219…       78            0 A          G         
#>  9       364 locus_22697… locus_226…      128            0 C          T         
#> 10       451 locus_26111… locus_261…       21            0 G          T         
#> # ℹ 71 more rows

# the same, from a subset of the loci table, with the missingness
hits <- show_loci(anole_gt) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(missing = missing) %>%
  dplyr::filter(missing > 0.6)
gt_lookup_loci(anole_gt, hits)
#> # A tibble: 81 × 8
#>    big_index name         chromosome position genetic_dist allele_ref allele_alt
#>        <int> <chr>        <chr>         <int>        <dbl> <chr>      <chr>     
#>  1        25 locus_2327_… locus_2327       59            0 A          C         
#>  2        71 locus_6428_… locus_6428       40            0 C          T         
#>  3        73 locus_6428_… locus_6428       42            0 T          G         
#>  4       236 locus_19280… locus_192…        4            0 G          T         
#>  5       254 locus_19654… locus_196…       88            0 C          A         
#>  6       255 locus_19654… locus_196…       89            0 C          A         
#>  7       256 locus_19654… locus_196…       90            0 A          T         
#>  8       349 locus_21964… locus_219…       78            0 A          G         
#>  9       364 locus_22697… locus_226…      128            0 C          T         
#> 10       451 locus_26111… locus_261…       21            0 G          T         
#> # ℹ 71 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: missing <dbl>

# the names of some chromosome codes
gt_lookup_chromosomes(anole_gt, c(1, 5, 5, NA))
#> [1] "locus_137" "locus_575" "locus_575" NA         

# put the original names back into the gen_tibble
anole_gt <- gt_restore_loci(anole_gt)
head(show_loci(anole_gt))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   big_index name         chromosome position genetic_dist allele_ref allele_alt
#>       <int> <chr>        <fct>         <int>        <dbl> <chr>      <chr>     
#> 1         1 locus_137_2  locus_137         2            0 G          A         
#> 2         2 locus_137_13 locus_137        13            0 A          G         
#> 3         3 locus_137_16 locus_137        16            0 T          C         
#> 4         4 locus_203_57 locus_203        57            0 G          A         
#> 5         5 locus_346_34 locus_346        34            0 T          C         
#> 6         6 locus_346_37 locus_346        37            0 A          C
